name: flask-ssti-syntax
rce_class: Template sink whose malformed syntax is answered differently (Jinja2)
notes: `syntax` was the last method with no case, and this closes it. The sink is
the shape the method was designed against, and the app is three lines of it:
`Template("Hello " + name).render()`, so the parameter is read as a Jinja2
template and nothing of the result has to be rendered for the oracle to
answer.
Measured by hand before the case was written, against vulhub flask/ssti on
2026-11-19: `?name={{7*7}}` answers 200 with 8 bytes, `Hello 49`; the same
pair with its closing delimiter gone, `?name={{7*7`, answers 500 with 290
bytes of Flask's own error page. That is a difference in the response's
*structure* -- a title and an h1 and a p where there was one text node --
which is what `response_shape` reads and what the whole differential rests
on.
Through the tool: `syntax-sink` on the `{{}}` form in all five contexts the
sink-shape ladder names, over 136 probes and 29 result rows, reported as
"the target answered structurally valid and structurally invalid {{}}
syntax differently, twice over on fresh operands".
The other 24 rows are `inconclusive`, and they are the reason this target
is worth more than one row. Jinja2 does not parse `${}`, `#{}`, `%{}`,
`<%= %>` or `@()`, so the app echoes those forms back verbatim -- `Hello
${4218*7591}` -- and the two halves of each pair then differ because the
*input* differed and not because anything parsed it. The reflection guard
says so and refuses to answer. So the case exercises the guard this oracle
most needs on the same target as the finding, in the same run: a response
that carries the probe back cannot be read as a parser, and a 500 that
carries nothing can.
Two shapes are disclosed as not tested rather than reported negative: the
`@()` form in the `shell_subshell` context, whose broken half that
context's own `)` suffix closes. 3.18.1 reported that `negative` and 3.18.2
stopped, which is the behaviour this case also pins.
The control is class attribution, the same shape as the Struts2 case and
the mirror of it. There, OGNL evaluates the value and no shell is behind
it; here, Jinja2 parses the value and no shell is behind it either, so the
shell-syntax probes of `reflected` have nothing to execute and nothing to
compute. Measured: 52 probes, all negative. A tool that confirmed there
would be flagging the parameter rather than the class.
`--environments python` pins the runtime the corpus records are written
for, which keeps the probe count stable between runs. `syntax` itself is
environment-blind -- a template delimiter is not a shell construct -- and
it deduplicates its waves per *context*, so the row count is the number of
contexts either way.
`share_target` is safe: both halves are GETs that read nothing and change
nothing on the target.
This case is **not** a CVE reproduction, and the advisory column for its
README row is empty on purpose. vulhub ships `flask/ssti` as a teaching
environment rather than a patched-and-unpatched pair, so what is proven
here is a method against real software -- which is worth recording, and
calling it a CVE would be the overclaim the coverage ledger exists to
avoid.
